page: Microsoft Azure FX4mds_v2 is a high-frequency, memory-dense virtual machine powered by the Intel Xeon 8573C processor under the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. Built on the x86_64 architecture, the instance provides 4 dedicated vCPUs across 2 physical cores with 2 threads per core, running at a high sustained clock speed of 4.2 GHz. The memory configuration is substantial, providing 84.0 GB of system RAM, which yields an allocation of 21.0 GB per vCPU. Hardware cache provisions include a 260 MB L3 cache, 2 MB L2 cache, and 48 KB L1d cache, supplemented by hardware support for AVX-512, AMX int8 and tile operations, and AES cryptography. Local storage is included as a 236 GB NVMe SSD. No GPU hardware or complimentary public IPv4 addresses are attached.

Benchmark results demonstrate exceptional single-thread performance driven by the 4.2 GHz base frequency. Geekbench single-core testing reached a top-tier score of 2262.0, while single-threaded data compression demonstrated strong performance with 34.59 GB/sec in gzip compression and 14.25 GB/sec in bzip3 decompression. However, aggregate parallel throughput reflects the limitation of having only 2 physical cores, resulting in lower relative rankings in multi-threaded stress-ng tests (4441.27) and Clang software compilation. Uncached large-block memory bandwidth benchmarks logged 35.98 GB/sec read and 25.58 GB/sec write speeds.

The combination of elevated per-core clock speed, extensive memory allocation per core, and bundled local NVMe storage delivers high resource density for specific bottleneck patterns. While multi-threaded compute capacity is limited by the vCPU count, the instance is well suited for memory-intensive workloads that rely heavily on single-thread frequency, including electronic design automation, financial modeling, in-memory caching systems, and database operations.
